cards.title: Product of powers with the same base

collision_audit.authority_caveat: This proposed label and collision audit do not confer canonical, alias, runtime, standards-mapping, assessment, or mastery authority.

cards.scope_rule: For a common base a and integer exponents m,n, multiply defined powers by adding exponents: a^m·a^n=a^(m+n). If any exponent is negative, require a≠0; exclude 0^0.
inclusions: integer exponents including positive, zero and negative
numeric and symbolic bases with declared domain
equivalent reciprocal form for negative resultant exponents
exclusions: undefined 0^0 or zero base with a negative exponent
automatic evidence for quotient, power-of-power, zero-exponent or negative-exponent atoms
boundary_conditions: zero resultant exponent is evaluated through the separate zero-exponent rule
negative resultant exponent is expressed through the separate reciprocal rule
zero base is allowed only when both input powers and the result are defined

misconceptions.mathematical_reason: multiplication concatenates equal factors, so counts add
misconceptions.remediation_target: expand a small example and count factors

misconceptions.mathematical_reason: the common base is not added
misconceptions.remediation_target: separate base value from factor count

misconceptions.mathematical_reason: a negative power contains division by a
misconceptions.remediation_target: rewrite as a reciprocal and inspect the denominator

assessment_evidence.rule: Mastery requires independent, unassisted evidence for this atom; an integrated response has one primary atom and cannot back-credit other atoms.
required: one zero-result case with nonzero base
one negative-result case with explicit a≠0
assessment_evidence.exact_oracle: canonicalize the integer exponent sum and, when negative, the mathematically equivalent reciprocal under the submitted domain restriction
independence: assessment variant and oracle are server-owned
guided steps, hints and worked answers are absent
equivalent mathematical forms are canonicalized before comparison
non_inference: does not prove quotient or power-of-power laws
does not independently prove zero or negative exponent meaning

reciprocal equivalence for a negative result

cards.scope_rule: For integer m,n and every defined expression, raise a power to a power by multiplying exponents: (a^m)^n=a^(mn). If n<0 or m<0, require a≠0; exclude 0^0.
inclusions: signed bases shown with unambiguous parentheses
positive, zero and negative products mn

inclusions: positive r with rational or irrational √r

returning only one branch for r>0
